raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

At decode, `batch_size` is the number of concurrent requests, so `_topk_topp_kernel`'s grid of `min(num_sm, batch_size)` programs puts a single-stream step on one compute unit, each program sweeping a whole vocabulary row serially. `topk_topp_triton.py` already splits rows across programs for top-p, but all three split stages begin with `if HAS_K and tl.load(K + row) < VOCAB_SIZE: return`, so rows with an active top-k keep the one-program-per-row grid. This adds a split pipeline that covers them. Its kernels are compiled at startup, and it only runs for batch shapes where it was measured to be faster than the existing kernel.

## Claims

- **End to end, Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 with its own sampling defaults** (`top_k=20, top_p=0.95`; one MI325X, TP1): median TPOT 1.1–1.9% lower at concurrency 1–16 and 0.9–1.0% lower at 32, in each of three rounds; output throughput 0.6–1.6% higher. At 64 the change is 0.3–1.8%. At 128, outside the gate, nothing changes.
- **The mask per decode step, measured inside the server:** 186.5 → 50.2 µs at 1 row, 222.4 → 63.3 µs at 8, 298.4 → 111.5 µs at 32.
- **Nothing compiles while serving.** The extraction loops run to a runtime bound, so 12 warmup variants cover every `k` up to 64. The first requests after startup see the same TTFT as main; engine startup takes about 7 s longer.
- **Accuracy unchanged.** gsm8k, sampled with the model's defaults, is 0.663 strict-match over 10 runs, against 0.662 for main built the same way and 0.668 for the official image, inside a run-to-run spread of up to 1.3 points. Inside the server, the masks from this path and from the existing kernel were identical on all 419,364 sampler rows after warm-up (same logits through both).
- **No slower shape is dispatched.** A row cap per bound on `k` and a vocabulary floor of 150,000, measured on real decode logits, keep every dispatched shape faster than the existing kernel. Other shapes, other platforms and callers that pass no bound run the existing kernel unchanged.
- **Correction to the first version of this description:** its gains at small vocabularies were measured against the existing kernel called with `has_topp_only_rows=True`, which also launches the no-op top-p split. MRv2 passes `False` for batches where every row has a top-k, and against that the split barely gains below 150,000 (see Which batches take it). All numbers here use `False`.

## Validation

### Tests

```bash
pytest -q tests/v1/sample/test_topk_split.py tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py
```

`37 passed`, and `119 passed, 37 skipped`, on MI325X. Added: the row cap follows `k`; a new `k` in the same tile compiles nothing; at 64 rows the split keeps exactly what a sort-based cut keeps.

### End-to-end serving

Both arms start from `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm72-edad8b03c5285a1c12e7e4f83c1af709b319a01b`, whose copies of the six files this PR touches are byte-identical to its merge base; the second arm is the same image with this PR's diff applied in place. Flags are the AMD ones from the Qwen3.5 recipe, identical in both arms:

```bash
VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER=1 vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8 --tensor-parallel-size 1 \
  --max-model-len 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8 --attention-backend ROCM_AITER_FA \
  --language-model-only
vllm bench serve --dataset-name random --random-input-len 1024 --random-output-len 256 \
  --ignore-eos --temperature 1.0 --top-k 20 --top-p 0.95 \
  --max-concurrency <c> --num-prompts <8c, at least 16> --seed 0
```

One MI325X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2, torch 2.13, Triton 3.8, AITER 0.1.26. Order main, this PR, main, this PR on the same GPU; every request completed with all 256 tokens.

| concurrency | median TPOT, main (ms) | median TPOT, this PR (ms) | change, round 1 / round 2 | output tok/s, round 1 / round 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 10.60 / 10.59 | 10.48 / 10.44 | −1.15% / −1.41% | +1.22% / +1.39% |
| 4 | 11.26 / 11.20 | 11.07 / 11.03 | −1.70% / −1.50% | +1.29% / +1.20% |
| 8 | 12.19 / 12.18 | 12.03 / 11.95 | −1.29% / −1.85% | +0.97% / +1.60% |
| 16 | 12.77 / 12.74 | 12.60 / 12.54 | −1.34% / −1.60% | +1.09% / +1.09% |
| 32 | 17.78 / 17.74 | 17.60 / 17.56 | −1.01% / −1.00% | +0.64% / +0.73% |
| 64 | 29.31 / 29.36 | 29.23 / 29.19 | −0.25% / −0.60% | +0.29% / +0.32% |
| 128 (outside the gate) | 54.57 / 54.64 | 54.67 / 54.50 | +0.18% / −0.26% | −0.20% / +0.31% |

Main against itself between rounds moved at most 0.50%, this PR against itself at most 0.65%. TTFT is unchanged at every concurrency.

The two rounds above were measured before the vocabulary floor was added, which does not change dispatch at this vocabulary (248320). A third round on the final commit, main then this PR: −1.40%, −1.33%, −1.69%, −1.09%, −0.92% and −1.84% at concurrency 1, 4, 8, 16, 32 and 64, and +0.22% at 128.

**First requests and startup.** The first 16 requests after startup (concurrency 8) have a median TTFT of 633–637 ms on this PR and 631–634 ms on main (p99 1118–1125 ms against 1115–1118 ms). vLLM's startup JIT warmup grows from 28 compile keys in 14.0–14.2 s to 40 in 19.8–20.0 s, and engine initialization from 93 s to 100 s.

### Accuracy

gsm8k, 5-shot, all 1319 questions, sampled with the model's defaults so that every decode step takes the top-k path (a profile during each run confirms it):

```bash
lm_eval --model local-completions --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 5 --batch_size 1 \
  --model_args model=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B-FP8,base_url=http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=32,tokenized_requests=False \
  --gen_kwargs temperature=1.0,top_p=0.95,top_k=20
```

| arm | runs | strict-match, mean (range) | flexible-extract, mean (range) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main, official image | 8 | 0.668 (0.658–0.676) | 0.693 (0.679–0.700) |
| main, rebuilt the way the PR image is | 4 | 0.662 (0.658–0.669) | 0.686 (0.679–0.692) |
| this PR | 10 | 0.663 (0.651–0.673) | 0.688 (0.672–0.699) |

Two runs of the same image on the same server differ by up to 1.3 points; with sampling on, generations differ run to run even for one image.

**Same logits through both kernels.** A debug build ran the existing kernel on a copy of every logits batch the split path masked, inside the server, during the runs above. After the first 250 sampler calls, all 419,364 rows had identical masks and kept values. Three rows within those first calls differed, from vLLM's startup sampler warm-up (`top_k=50, top_p=0.9`) and the benchmark warm-up's random-token prompts. Checked against an exact sort-based top-k/top-p cut on the saved input logits, this path matched each time, and the existing kernel kept or dropped a token at the top-p boundary.

### Inside the server

torch profiler on the same server and model, one decode iteration from one `_gumbel_sample_kernel` to the next (median); the mask is every kernel between the first top-k kernel and `_gumbel_sample_kernel`:

| rows per step | mask, main | mask, this PR | kernels in the mask, this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 186.5 µs | 50.2 µs | chunk, combine, fill, scatter |
| 8 | 222.4 µs | 63.3 µs | |
| 32 | 298.4 µs | 111.5 µs | |

The GPU is idle for about 29 µs per iteration in both arms, so the time the mask saves comes off the step.

## Details

### Root cause

`_build_dispatch` launches one program per row, capped at one per SM:

```python
num_programs = min(num_sm, batch_size)
```

Each program then sweeps its row in `BLOCK_SIZE` tiles, and the comment above the launch already names the consequence — "per-tile latency bounds kernel latency". The existing "Split-row pipeline for small batches" solves exactly this by giving a row to several programs, but it is a top-p machine: `K` reaches its three stage kernels only so that rows with an active top-k can `return` immediately. So there is no top-k capability in it to widen a gate into.

### Design

Top-k makes the row easier to split rather than harder, because top-k is applied before top-p: at `k=20` at most twenty logits survive, so the result is a scatter over known indices rather than a threshold comparison across the row. Four kernels:

1. **Per-chunk top-k** (`_topk_split_chunk_kernel`, grid `(rows, chunks)`) — each program extracts its own chunk's top-`k` by repeated max from registers. Exact, not approximate: an element of the global top-k is at least as large as every element of its own chunk bar at most k−1 of them, so it cannot hide from its chunk's top-k.
2. **Merge and cut** (`_topk_split_combine_kernel`, grid `(rows,)`) — merges the chunk candidates, cuts at that row's own `k`, applies top-p to the survivors.
3. **Scatter** — `fill_` then `scatter_` over the survivors.

Candidates are retired by index rather than by value, which keeps duplicate logits emitted once each, and is why tied rows match the reference.

**Compilation.** The bound on `k` is a runtime argument in `do_not_specialize`, and the only compile-time choices are the candidate tile (16, 32 or 64) and whether top-p is on, so each kernel has 6 variants. Both go through `triton_kernel_dispatcher_with_warmup` and are registered in `register_top_k_top_p_warmups` on ROCm. The chunk kernel loops to the bound; the merge is unrolled over the tile with a runtime guard, because a plain loop is slower there.

<details>
<summary>One non-obvious choice: the top-p cut is written on the suffix mass</summary>

```python
suffix = tl.flip(tl.cumsum(tl.flip(e, 0), 0), 0)
kept = head & (suffix > (1.0 - p) * total)
```

The direct prefix form saturates. A peaked row's running exclusive prefix mass reaches exactly 1.0 in float32 after about seventeen terms, so `prefix < p` is false for `p = 1.0` and silently truncates a row that asked for no top-p filtering at all. `get_top_k_top_p` only drops the `p` tensor when *every* row is 1.0, so a mixed batch carries such rows in. The suffix form compares against `(1 - p) * total`, which is exactly 0 at `p = 1.0`, and keeps the row whole. `test_matches_reference_across_p` covers `p = 1.0` for this reason.

</details>

### Which batches take it

| bound on `k` | most rows |
|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | 64 |
| ≤ 32 | 32 |
| ≤ 40 | 16 |
| ≤ 48 | 8 |
| ≤ 64 | 4 |

Measured on 768 decode rows of Qwen3-0.6B (vocabulary 151936) with each bound as every row's `k`; on Gemma 3 decode rows (262144) and at 248320 every capped shape wins with more margin. Past a row's cap the merge and the extra launches cost more than the split saves.

The split also needs a vocabulary of at least 150,000. Below that the monolithic kernel is cheap enough that the split loses at some capped shapes, for example 0.72x at vocabulary 32064 with `k=20` at 64 rows, and 0.57x with `k=64` at 4 rows. Every model I found that ships a `top_k` default (Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 with 20, MiniMax-M2 with 40, Gemma 3 and 4 with 64) has a vocabulary above that. The warmup is skipped for smaller vocabularies.

### Where the bound on k comes from

The candidate tile is a compile-time constant, so the pipeline needs an upper bound on every row's `k`. Taking it from the `k` tensor would be a device sync on the execution thread. `get_top_k_top_p` already reads a host mirror, `top_k_np`, and already derives `has_topp_only_rows` from it, so `max_top_k` follows the same route and costs nothing. It is threaded through the same call chain as `has_topp_only_rows`, and defaults to `None`, which selects the existing behaviour.

### Complexity

283 lines in `topk_topp_triton.py` and 54 across `topk_topp_sampler.py` and the four callers that pass the bound, tests excluded. The 283 are the two kernels, their warmup-registered dispatchers, the launch helper and the row cap. The split costs four launches where the monolithic kernel needs one, which is why it is limited to the shapes in the table above.

### Overlapping work

- #62594 also split the sweeps of rows with an active top-k across programs, on CUDA, by adding split branches to the monolithic kernel itself; its author closed it after measuring 0.5% lower TPOT at 128 rows per step. This PR leaves the monolithic kernel unchanged, adds a separate pipeline for ROCm only, and caps it at 64 rows.
- #62596 changes the monolithic kernel's top-k pivot (#61998). It does not touch this path; the main column above will move when it lands, and I will measure again.
- #54651 and #61996 are the top-p split pipeline this mirrors.

### Limitations

- **A batch with any greedy or top-p-only row falls through entirely.** `max_top_k` is the max over all rows, and such a row carries `k = vocab_size`. Leaving greedy rows out of the bound would keep mixed traffic on this path; it is a follow-up.
- **The two paths can disagree at the top-p boundary**, because the existing kernel's pivot search is approximate. In the cases found, this path matched an exact sort-based cut and the existing kernel did not. On a row with no variance at all the existing kernel masks nothing, while this path keeps `k`; `test_a_zero_variance_row_diverges_from_the_reference` records it.
- **Gated to ROCm and measured on gfx942 (MI325X) only**, and the row cap was measured on that GPU.
- **Not wired into the V1 runner** (`TopKTopPSampler`) or the V1 rejection sampler, which call `apply_top_k_top_p` without the bound.
- **This is a second implementation beside the existing split pipeline**, which the contribution guide discourages. Teaching that pipeline to apply top-k would be the unified design; it is a substantially larger change.

---

<details>
<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity.
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

The suffix form compares against `(1 - p) * total`, which is exactly 0 at `p = 1.0`, and keeps the row whole. `test_matches_reference_across_p` covers `p = 1.0` for this reason.

</details>

### Which batches take it

| bound on `k` | most rows |
|---|---|
| ≤ 24 | 64 |
| ≤ 32 | 32 |
| ≤ 40 | 16 |
| ≤ 48 | 8 |
| ≤ 64 | 4 |

Measured on 768 decode rows of Qwen3-0.6B (vocabulary 151936) with each bound as every row's `k`; on Gemma 3 decode rows (262144) and at 248320 every capped shape wins with more margin. Past a row's cap the merge and the extra launches cost more than the split saves.

The split also needs a vocabulary of at least 150,000. Below that the monolithic kernel is cheap enough that the split loses at some capped shapes, for example 0.72x at vocabulary 32064 with `k=20` at 64 rows, and 0.57x with `k=64` at 4 rows. Every model I found that ships a `top_k` default (Qwen3, Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.8 with 20, MiniMax-M2 with 40, Gemma 3 and 4 with 64) has a vocabulary above that. The warmup is skipped for smaller vocabularies.

### Where the bound on k comes from

The candidate tile is a compile-time constant, so the pipeline needs an upper bound on every row's `k`. Taking it from the `k` tensor would be a device sync on the execution thread. `get_top_k_top_p` already reads a host mirror, `top_k_np`, and already derives `has_topp_only_rows` from it, so `max_top_k` follows the same route and costs nothing. It is threaded through the same call chain as `has_topp_only_rows`, and defaults to `None`, which selects the existing behaviour.

### Complexity

283 lines in `topk_topp_triton.py` and 54 across `topk_topp_sampler.py` and the four callers that pass the bound, tests excluded. The 283 are the two kernels, their warmup-registered dispatchers, the launch helper and the row cap. The split costs four launches where the monolithic kernel needs one, which is why it is limited to the shapes in the table above.

### Overlapping work

- #62594 also split the sweeps of rows with an active top-k across programs, on CUDA, by adding split branches to the monolithic kernel itself; its author closed it after measuring 0.5% lower TPOT at 128 rows per step. This PR leaves the monolithic kernel unchanged, adds a separate pipeline for ROCm only, and caps it at 64 rows.
- #62596 changes the monolithic kernel's top-k pivot (#61998). It does not touch this path; the main column above will move when it lands, and I will measure again.
- #54651 and #61996 are the top-p split pipeline this mirrors.

### Limitations

- **A batch with any greedy or top-p-only row falls through entirely.** `max_top_k` is the max over all rows, and such a row carries `k = vocab_size`. Leaving greedy rows out of the bound would keep mixed traffic on this path; it is a follow-up.
- **The two paths can disagree at the top-p boundary**, because the existing kernel's pivot search is approximate. In the cases found, this path matched an exact sort-based cut and the existing kernel did not. On a row with no variance at all the existing kernel masks nothing, while this path keeps `k`; `test_a_zero_variance_row_diverges_from_the_reference` records it.
- **Gated to ROCm and measured on gfx942 (MI325X) only**, and the row cap was measured on that GPU.
- **Not wired into the V1 runner** (`TopKTopPSampler`) or the V1 rejection sampler, which call `apply_top_k_top_p` without the bound.
- **This is a second implementation beside the existing split pipeline**, which the contribution guide discourages. Teaching that pipeline to apply top-k would be the unified design; it is a substantially larger change.

+VOCAB = 32768  # over _TOPK_SPLIT_MIN_VOCAB, small enough to keep tests quick
+DEVICE = "cuda"

+def _logits(rows: int, seed: int, scale: float = 4.0) -> torch.Tensor:
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(seed)

+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("p_val", [0.1, 0.5, 0.9, 0.99, 1.0])
+def test_matches_reference_across_p(p_val):

+    p = torch.full((2,), p_val, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)

+
+
+def test_matches_reference_with_mixed_per_row_params():
+    k = torch.tensor([1, 20, 7, 64], dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)

+    _assert_identical(*_both(_logits(4, 3), k, p))
+
+
+def test_matches_reference_without_top_p():
+    k = torch.full((4,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)

+
+
+def test_matches_reference_on_tied_logits():
+    """Duplicates must be emitted once each, not retired together."""
+    logits = _logits(2, 5)
+    logits[:, :64] = 3.5  # far more ties than any row's k
+    k = torch.full((2,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((2,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
+    _assert_identical(*_both(logits, k, p))
+
+
+def test_matches_reference_with_masked_rows():
+    """Grammar masks leave rows mostly -inf."""
+    logits = _logits(2, 6)
+    logits[0, 100:] = float("-inf")
+    logits[1, :-100] = float("-inf")
+    k = torch.full((2,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((2,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)

+
+
+def test_a_zero_variance_row_diverges_from_the_reference():
+    """The one input where the two paths disagree, recorded rather than hidden.
+
+    On a row with no variance at all the reference masks nothing, so more than
+    k tokens survive top_k; the split path keeps k and then applies top-p to

+    is where the reference's normal-approximation pivot search has no spread to

+    """
+    logits = torch.zeros(2, VOCAB, device=DEVICE, dtype=torch.float32)

+    p = torch.full((2,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)

+
+
+def test_the_split_path_is_actually_taken():

+    Without this, a gate that silently declines every case would still show

+    """

+
+    import vllm.v1.sample.ops.topk_topp_triton as mod
+
+    k = torch.full((2,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((2,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)

+        assert spy.call_count == 1
+        apply_top_k_top_p_triton(_logits(2, 8), k, p, max_top_k=None)
+        assert spy.call_count == 1, "max_top_k=None must stay on the reference"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.parametrize(
+    "max_top_k,reason",
+    [
+        (_TOPK_SPLIT_MAX_K + 1, "k past the candidate cap"),
+        (0, "k below one"),
+    ],
+)
+def test_declines_outside_its_bounds(max_top_k, reason):
+    """Unsupported bounds fall through rather than answering approximately."""
+    rows = 2
+    k = torch.full((rows,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((rows,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
+    logits = _logits(rows, 9)
+    ref = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(logits.clone(), k, p, max_top_k=None)
+    out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(logits.clone(), k, p, max_top_k=max_top_k)
+    _assert_identical(ref, out)
+
+
+def test_declines_a_vocabulary_too_small_to_benefit():
+    rows, small = 2, _TOPK_SPLIT_MIN_VOCAB // 2
+    g = torch.Generator(device=DEVICE).manual_seed(10)
+    logits = torch.randn(rows, small, generator=g, device=DEVICE) * 4
+    k = torch.full((rows,), 20, dtype=torch.int32, device=DEVICE)
+    p = torch.full((rows,), 0.95, dtype=torch.float32, device=DEVICE)
+    ref = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(logits.clone(), k, p, max_top_k=None)
+    out = apply_top_k_top_p_triton(logits.clone(), k, p, max_top_k=20)
+    _assert_identical(ref, out)

     )
 
 
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+# Split-row top-k pipeline for small batches.
+# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
+
+# Candidates kept per chunk, so the merge tile is CHUNKS * this. Past it the
+# monolithic kernel's single pass is the better shape.
+_TOPK_SPLIT_MAX_K = 64
+# Pieces the vocabulary is cut into. Raising it widens the merge tile faster
+# than it shortens each program's sweep.
+_TOPK_SPLIT_CHUNKS = 128
+_TOPK_SPLIT_MAX_BATCH = 64
+# Below this one program is not actually starved, and three launches cost more
+# than they save.
+_TOPK_SPLIT_MIN_VOCAB = 8192
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_split_chunk_kernel(
+    LOGITS,
+    LOGITS_STRIDE_0,
+    CAND_V,
+    CAND_I,
+    VOCAB,
+    CHUNK: tl.constexpr,
+    CHUNKS: tl.constexpr,
+    KCAP: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Each chunk's own top-KCAP logits and their indices, ties by lowest index.
+
+    Grid is (rows, CHUNKS). Writes [rows, CHUNKS * KCAP] float32 values and
+    int32 indices. A row's k largest elements cannot hide from this: an element
+    of the global top-k is at least as large as every element of its own chunk
+    bar at most k-1 of them.
+    """
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    chunk = tl.program_id(1)
+    base = chunk * CHUNK
+
+    lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    offs = base + lane
+    # BLOCK is rounded up to a power of two, so it can reach past both the
+    # chunk and the row; both bounds are needed or a chunk takes its
+    # neighbour's elements.
+    live = (lane < CHUNK) & (offs < VOCAB)
+    vals = tl.load(
+        LOGITS + row.to(tl.int64) * LOGITS_STRIDE_0 + offs,
+        mask=live,
+        other=float("-inf"),
+    )
+    # VOCAB doubles as the "no such index" sentinel: it sorts above every real
+    # index under tl.min, so a tie is won by the lowest real index.
+    idxs = tl.where(live, offs, VOCAB)
+
+    out = (row * CHUNKS + chunk) * KCAP
+    for i in tl.static_range(KCAP):
+        best = tl.max(vals, 0)
+        at = tl.min(tl.where(vals == best, idxs, VOCAB), 0)
+        tl.store(CAND_V + out + i, best)
+        tl.store(CAND_I + out + i, at)
+        # Retire by index rather than by value, so duplicates are emitted once
+        # each instead of vanishing together.
+        vals = tl.where(idxs == at, float("-inf"), vals)
+
+
+@triton.jit
+def _topk_split_combine_kernel(
+    CAND_V,
+    CAND_I,
+    K,
+    P,
+    KEEP_V,
+    KEEP_I,
+    VOCAB,
+    NUM_CAND: tl.constexpr,
+    KCAP: tl.constexpr,
+    BLOCK: tl.constexpr,
+    TOPP_ENABLED: tl.constexpr,
+):
+    """Merge the per-chunk candidates, cut at the row's k, then apply top-p.
+
+    Grid is (rows,). Writes [rows, KCAP] survivors; positions that did not
+    survive repeat position zero, so the scatter has no invalid index to guard.
+    """
+    row = tl.program_id(0)
+    lane = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
+    live = lane < NUM_CAND
+    vals = tl.load(CAND_V + row * NUM_CAND + lane, mask=live, other=float("-inf"))
+    idxs = tl.load(CAND_I + row * NUM_CAND + lane, mask=live, other=VOCAB)
+
+    k = tl.minimum(tl.load(K + row), KCAP)
+
+    # Triton cannot index a register tile with a loop variable, so each
+    # extracted element is placed by a predicate.
+    sorted_v = tl.full((BLOCK,), float("-inf"), tl.float32)
+    sorted_i = tl.full((BLOCK,), VOCAB, tl.int32)
+    for i in tl.static_range(KCAP):
+        best = tl.max(vals, 0)
+        at = tl.min(tl.where(vals == best, idxs, VOCAB), 0)
+        sorted_v = tl.where(lane == i, best, sorted_v)
+        sorted_i = tl.where(lane == i, at, sorted_i)
+        vals = tl.where(idxs == at, float("-inf"), vals)
+
+    head = (lane < k) & (sorted_i < VOCAB)
+    v = tl.where(head, sorted_v, float("-inf"))
+
+    if TOPP_ENABLED:
+        p = tl.load(P + row)
+        e = tl.where(head, tl.exp(v - tl.max(v, 0)), 0.0)
+        total = tl.sum(e, 0)
+        # Keep a token when the mass strictly before it is under p, written as
+        # a condition on the mass from it onward. The direct prefix form
+        # saturates: a peaked row's running prefix reaches exactly 1.0 in
+        # float32 after about seventeen terms, and `1.0 < p` is then false for
+        # p = 1, truncating a row that asked for no top-p filtering at all.
+        suffix = tl.flip(tl.cumsum(tl.flip(e, 0), 0), 0)
+        kept = head & (suffix > (1.0 - p) * total)
+    else:
+        kept = head
+
+    first_v = tl.sum(tl.where(lane == 0, sorted_v, 0.0), 0)
+    first_i = tl.sum(tl.where(lane == 0, sorted_i, 0), 0)
+    store = lane < KCAP
+    tl.store(KEEP_V + row * KCAP + lane, tl.where(kept, sorted_v, first_v), mask=store)
+    tl.store(
+        KEEP_I + row * KCAP + lane,
+        tl.where(kept, sorted_i, first_i).to(tl.int64),
+        mask=store,
+    )
+
+
+def _apply_topk_split(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    k: torch.Tensor,
+    p: torch.Tensor | None,
+    max_top_k: int,
+    mask_value: float,
+) -> None:
+    """Split-row top-k/top-p pipeline for small batches; masks in place."""
+    rows, vocab = logits.shape
+    chunk = triton.cdiv(vocab, _TOPK_SPLIT_CHUNKS)
+    num_cand = _TOPK_SPLIT_CHUNKS * max_top_k
+
+    cand_v = logits.new_empty((rows, num_cand))
+    cand_i = logits.new_empty((rows, num_cand), dtype=torch.int32)
+    _topk_split_chunk_kernel[(rows, _TOPK_SPLIT_CHUNKS)](
+        logits,
+        logits.stride(0),
+        cand_v,
+        cand_i,
+        vocab,
+        CHUNK=chunk,
+        CHUNKS=_TOPK_SPLIT_CHUNKS,
+        KCAP=max_top_k,
+        BLOCK=next_power_of_2(chunk),
+        num_warps=4,
+    )
+
+    keep_v = logits.new_empty((rows, max_top_k))
+    keep_i = logits.new_empty((rows, max_top_k), dtype=torch.int64)
+    _topk_split_combine_kernel[(rows,)](
+        cand_v,
+        cand_i,
+        k,
+        p if p is not None else cand_v,
+        keep_v,
+        keep_i,
+        vocab,
+        NUM_CAND=num_cand,
+        KCAP=max_top_k,
+        BLOCK=next_power_of_2(num_cand),
+        TOPP_ENABLED=p is not None,
+        num_warps=8,
+    )
+
+    # Ordering across launches is what keeps the fill from erasing the scatter.
+    logits.fill_(mask_value)
+    logits.scatter_(-1, keep_i, keep_v)
+
+
 def apply_top_k_top_p_triton(
     logits: torch.Tensor,
     k: torch.Tensor | None,
     p: torch.Tensor | None,
     mask_value: float = float("-inf"),
     has_topp_only_rows: bool = True,
+    max_top_k: int | None = None,
 ) -> torch.Tensor:
     """Apply combined top-k and top-p masking using Triton.

         has_topp_only_rows: Whether any row has p < 1 and k >= vocab_size.
             False lets small batches skip the split top-p pipeline; pass it
             only if no such row exists, as such a row would get no top-p.
+        max_top_k: An upper bound on every row's k, or None if unknown. Lets
+            small batches take the split top-k pipeline, whose per-chunk
+            candidate count is a compile-time constant. Callers holding a host
+            mirror of top_k can supply it without a device sync.
 
     Returns:
         The masked logits tensor. It may or may not be modified in-place.
@@ -1685,6 +1870,25 @@ def apply_top_k_top_p_triton(
         _apply_topp_split(logits, None, p_ptr, mask_value, num_sm)
